commit.message: chore(js): baseline the import-block clones moved by the #128 changes
style(experiments): format the issue #128 server-close experiment
docs: follow a GitHub docs redirect and stop link-checking browser-internal URLs

test(js): exit with a real process so command-stream does not echo the error

command-stream's virtual exit builtin writes 'Command failed with exit code 7'
to stderr even when the rejection is caught, leaving a stray error-looking line
at the end of every CI test log (#128). The experiment reproduces it.

fix(python): close the sqlite3 connections the tests open, and fail on a leak

`with sqlite3.connect(...)` commits but never closes, so one test leaked a
connection that the next test's warnings summary reported as a
ResourceWarning; CI passed regardless. The fixtures now use
contextlib.closing(), and pytest turns ResourceWarning and unraisable
exceptions into errors. Part of #128.

test(js): share the command-stream test preamble instead of cloning it

The switch to a real process for the exit-code test made jscpd report the
load/skip/rejects sequence as a new clone. itWithShell holds it once.

fix(ci): prove each registry accepts the publish before building the release

Run 37509328334 built, tested and versioned the Python package on main and
only then failed at "Publish to PyPI" with invalid-publisher. A
release-preflight job now performs the credential half of each publish
(PyPI and npm OIDC token exchange, crates.io token check) in parallel with
lint and tests. On main and manual releases a refusal fails the run and the
publishing jobs require the preflight to succeed; on pull requests it only
annotates. Principle 16 of the link-foundation pipeline templates, with
three corrections: PyPI's 422 invalid-publisher counts as a refusal, a
crates.io 403 for an API token on /api/v1/me is read by its reason (rust
template #183), and curl's 000 is unreachable rather than a status.
Part of #128.

fix(ci): pin Linux jobs to ubuntu-24.04 and reject the moving ubuntu-latest label

Every Linux job carried "The ubuntu-latest label will migrate to Ubuntu 26
beginning October 19, 2026" (actions/runner-images#14748), and the
migration would change the OS under every job unannounced. All 62 uses,
including the matrix.os conditions that pick the coverage upload, now name
ubuntu-24.04, and check-ci-workflows rejects ubuntu-latest on any
non-comment line. Same change as the pipeline templates (js#193, rust#180,
python#89). Part of #128.

fix(ci): audit workflows at zizmor's low confidence and fix what it hid

The zizmor job ran with --min-confidence medium. artipacked and
template-injection both report at low confidence, so the job was green
while 38 checkouts left the job token in .git/config and 10 run: blocks
expanded step outputs straight into shell text.

- check-ci-workflows.mjs now rejects a checkout without
  persist-credentials: false, and allows true only in a main-writer job.
  The four release jobs that push keep true with a comment; changeset-pr
  does not need it, because create-pull-request configures its own token.
- Step outputs reach the shell through env: instead of ${{ }}.
- zizmor runs at low confidence, pinned to 1.30.1 rather than the
  action's moving "latest", plus a pedantic high/high pass for
  unpinned-images, as in the js pipeline template.
- The actionlint image and the no-openssl container are pinned by digest.

Evidence: dev/log/issues/128/pulls/129/reproductions/zizmor-low-confidence-*.log
Refs #128

fix(ci): fail cargo audit on advisory warnings and pin the secretlint run

cargo audit prints unmaintained, unsound and yanked advisories as
warnings and exits 0, so security.yml would pass a lockfile carrying
one. --deny warnings makes them fail; rust/Cargo.lock has none today.

secretlint ran as `npx --yes -p secretlint`, i.e. whatever release is
newest when CI starts. It is pinned to 13.0.7. A planted token probe
confirms the silent step is a real scan, not a false negative.

check-ci-workflows.mjs rejects both regressions: an unpinned `npx -p`
package and a `cargo audit` without --deny warnings.

Refs #128

fix(ci): annotate the skipped Pages deployment instead of echoing it

Pages is not enabled for this repository (GET /repos/.../pages is 404)
and DEPLOY_GITHUB_PAGES is unset, so every main push builds the docs and
publishes nothing. The skip step only echoed that into a collapsed log;
it is now a ::notice annotation on the run summary.

Refs #128

chore(log): drop duplicated main-run logs from the issue #128 evidence

The security and quality logs of the main run were already saved under
ci-logs/; point the secretlint probe at that copy.

Refs #128

fix(ci): bump zizmor-action to v0.6.4, the first release that can install zizmor 1.30.1

zizmor-action resolves `version:` against its own digest table and dies
with "Unknown version" for anything newer; v0.6.2 stops at 1.29.0, so
the 1.30.1 pin from the low-confidence change would have failed the job.
Its `latest` is that table's entry, not the newest zizmor, so the comment
claiming a moving default is corrected too. A test now keeps the action,
the pipx pass and the reproduce comment on one version the action knows.

docs(log): record the upstream reports filed for issue #128

command-stream#213 (virtual exit echoes its error to stderr), rust
template #185 and #186, python template #95 and js template #209 and
#210, each with the filed body and the reproduction it rests on.
docs(log): add the signal classification, template comparison and PR CI logs for issue #128

fix(ci): attribute release commits to the github-actions[bot] account

The six places that configure the CI commit author used
github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com, which matches no account,
so release commits were unattributed. A ruleset with
require_extra_approval_for_unattributed_changes would hold every
automated release for manual approval. Use the numeric-prefixed
address, as the JS pipeline template now does, and add a test that
fails on any tracked unprefixed occurrence.

fix(js): print only the clones the duplication gate fails on

With the console reporter, jscpd --baseline --fail-on-new-clones lists
every clone it finds. Each passing run therefore logged 272 'Clone found'
blocks (843 lines) for clones the baseline already accepts, and the
clone that failed a run was marked only by a [NEW] tag inside that list.
check:duplication now runs jscpd with the JSON reporter and prints the
new clones (as error annotations on the repository path in GitHub
Actions) plus a one-line total. It fails closed when jscpd writes no
report.

fix(ci): fail the status gate on cancellations no supersede explains

The gate raised cancelled jobs as errors only on main pushes that were
still the branch head. On pull request branches every cancellation,
including a job killed by its timeout-minutes, was a warning and the
run passed. On superseded main runs it also excused writers declared
with cancel-in-progress: false, which a newer run queues behind rather
than cancels.

A cancellation is now excused only when the branch head has moved past
the run AND the job's effective cancel-in-progress is literally true,
as in the link-foundation pipeline templates. The per-job value is read
from the running workflow (GITHUB_WORKFLOW_REF) by
scripts/read-job-cancel-in-progress.mjs; anything unreadable fails
closed. Pull request runs pass the head commit and head branch, since
github.sha is a merge commit no branch points at.
PIPELINE_STATUS_VERBOSE=1 traces each decision.

Part of #128.

fix(ci): persist the lychee cache that --cache already asked for

links.yml ran lychee with --cache --max-cache-age 1d, but .lycheecache
lives in the workspace and nothing restored it, so every run re-checked
every link. Restore and save it with actions/cache, as the lychee-action
README recommends, and test that the cache step precedes lychee.

Part of #128.

docs(test): state what the bot e-mail change does and does not fix

c744aae said the legacy github-actions[bot] no-reply address left
release commits unattributed. The commits API attributes this
repository's legacy-address release commits to github-actions[bot], so
that claim (taken from the JS template's #144) does not hold here.
Keep the documented 41898282+ form and record the evidence.

Part of #128.

fix(scripts): use forward-slash virtual paths so the Puppeteer API parser works on Windows

TypeScript 7's createVirtualFileSystem looks files up by exact key, and the
native compiler asks for them with forward slashes. path.join built the keys
with backslashes on Windows, so tsconfig.json was never found and
snapshot.getProject() returned undefined (PR run 37526767522). The test that
exposed it only began running in 5925ee5, which stopped it from skipping.

fix(ci): run the real-browser suites that no workflow ran

Ten end-to-end suites skip without RUN_E2E (or are #[ignore]d), and no
workflow ran them, so CI stayed green whatever they did (issue #128). parity.yml
now runs nine of them: the click-readiness, downloads and traces suites in a new
engine-suites job, the Playwright and Puppeteer suites against the React fixture
in a new fixture-suites job, and the headful Python launches and Rust launch and
connect smokes in snapshots. Each run fails when a suite skips or asserts
nothing. The Google sign-in probe stays manual: it drives a third-party site.

e2e-suite-coverage.test.js fails when a suite is neither run by a workflow nor
listed as manual-only with a reason. parity.yml's gate also moves to the
RUN_SHA/BRANCH_NAME inputs every other workflow uses since fa75f97, and its
checkouts no longer persist credentials.
docs(log): add the timeline, requirements, root causes and sources for issue #128

test(js): compare the PyPI registration URL whole instead of as a substring

CodeQL's js/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization flagged
output.includes(PENDING_PUBLISHER_URL). The test now extracts the URL the
preflight prints and compares it exactly.

fix(scripts): let command-stream quote the JS release commit message

version-and-commit.mjs escaped " by hand and wrapped the value in quotes.
command-stream already quotes interpolations, so a hand-escaped quote reached
git as a literal backslash (experiments/issue-128/command-stream-quoting.mjs).
CodeQL reported it as js/incomplete-sanitization. The Rust script already used
a bare interpolation; the JS one now does too, and a test keeps hand escaping
out of both release script directories.

fix(selectors): parse Playwright text selectors in linear time

/^(.+?):has-text\("(.+?)"\)$/ backtracks quadratically on a long selector
that does not match: 16s for 550,000 characters in JS and 48s for 220,000 in
Python (experiments/issue-128/text-selector-redos.mjs). CodeQL reported the JS
copies as js/polynomial-redos. Both languages now split the selector with
indexOf/find and endsWith, keeping the lazy regex's choice of the first
pseudo-class as the split point.

chore(js): fold the selector note into the PR's single changeset

validate-changeset.mjs allows one changeset per pull request.

fix(tests): trim artifact names without a backtracking regex

sanitizeArtifactName kept literal dashes and then trimmed with /^-+|-+$/g,
which backtracks quadratically on a long inner run: 4s for 50,000 dashes.
CodeQL reported it as js/polynomial-redos. The trim now walks the string from
both ends.

fix(scripts): recognise formatted release notes by their npm badge

format-release-notes.mjs skipped any body containing img.shields.io, so a
changelog that mentions the host would never be formatted. CodeQL reported
the host substring check as js/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization. The
check now looks for the badge markup the script itself appends, built from
the same constant. Both checks agree on every published release.

test(rust): name the coordinate range errors for what they hold

rejects_out_of_range_coordinates bound the two errors to variables named
latitude and longitude, and CodeQL's name-based rust/cleartext-logging read
the assert messages as logging location data. They are now north_south_error
and east_west_error.

test(rust): derive the cookie fixture key and name Chrome's fixed IV

CodeQL's rust/hard-coded-cryptographic-value read the zeroed output buffer
handed to pbkdf2_hmac as a hard-coded key, and the inline [0x20; 16] as a
hard-coded IV. The fixture now takes the key from pbkdf2_hmac_array and
passes the IV as CHROME_CBC_IV through new_from_slices, as the library's
own encryptor does. The ciphertext is byte-for-byte unchanged
(experiments/issue-128/cookie-fixture-equivalence).

test(rust): expect the about:blank start URL in the headful smoke

4dc6743 made launch_real_browser append START_URL (about:blank) to the
command line and updated the unit tests, but the #[ignore]d smoke kept the
old two-argument list. No workflow ran it until the parity job wired the
ignored Rust smokes in, so it failed for the first time on this PR.
chore(log): keep the failed PR runs and the Safari retry reproduction

fix(js): start a fresh safaridriver when a back-to-back Safari launch fails

safaridriver serves one automation session at a time. In three of the
last seven Safari runs on this PR, a launch right after a previous session
closed failed: the new driver exited with code 1 before it was ready
(run 37533483103), or answered /status and then refused the new-session
request with ECONNREFUSED (runs 37525917388, 37533921118).

Safari launches now retry those start-up failures with a fresh driver, up
to three attempts, one second apart. Authorization errors are not retried.
A refused connection also names the driver server and whether it had
exited, so the next failure says more than a port. VERBOSE=1 logs each
retry.

fix(python): start a fresh safaridriver when a back-to-back Safari launch fails

Same start-up race as the JavaScript launcher: retry a Safari launch whose
driver exits before it is ready or refuses the connection, up to three
attempts. Authorization errors are not retried.

fix(rust): start a fresh safaridriver when a back-to-back Safari launch fails

Same start-up race as the JavaScript launcher: retry a Safari launch whose
driver exits before it is ready or refuses the connection, up to three
attempts. SafariSetupError is not retried.
docs(log): record the CodeQL, smoke and Safari findings

test(js): share the use-m reachability probe instead of cloning it

d6a0451 added imports to command-stream-errexit.test.js, which moved jscpd's
window onto the hasNetwork() helper it shares with
use-module-integration.test.js, and the duplication gate failed (run
37537484417). isUseMReachable() in scripts/use-module.mjs now holds it once.

test(js): spell out the hand-escaped commit message instead of escaping it

The test and experiment that show why version-and-commit.mjs must not escape
quotes by hand re-created that escaping with .replace(/"/g, ...), and CodeQL
flagged them as new js/incomplete-sanitization alerts (PR alerts 63, 64).
The escaped value is now a literal fixture, which is what the test means.
docs(log): record the duplication and CodeQL follow-ups

test(experiments): check the cookie fixture against the recorded old ciphertext

The equivalence experiment rebuilt the pre-3a31c23 fixture, zeroed key buffer
and inline IV included, so CodeQL raised rust/hard-coded-cryptographic-value
on it (PR alerts 65, 66). It now compares the new fixture with the ciphertext
the old code produced, as recorded in the reproduction log; the output is the
same.
style(experiments): rustfmt the cookie fixture experiment

commit.message:
Verify the crates.io token fallback in the release preflight

The release preflight gates the publishers, so it refused releases that
the token fallback could still publish. When the trusted publishing
exchange fails and CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN or CARGO_TOKEN is set, the
preflight now sends a publish request without an archive: crates.io
checks the token and its scope for the crate before it reads the
archive, so "invalid tarball length" proves the token can publish and
nothing is uploaded. A verified fallback passes with a warning; release
mode blocks only when neither credential can publish.

The workflow tests now assert the fallback policy instead of OIDC-only.

+name: CI Workflow Policy
+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches:
+      - main
+    paths:
+      - '.github/workflows/**'
+      - '.github/zizmor.yml'
+      - 'scripts/check-ci-workflows.mjs'
+  pull_request:
+    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
+    paths:
+      - '.github/workflows/**'
+      - '.github/zizmor.yml'
+      - 'scripts/check-ci-workflows.mjs'
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+env:
+  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
+  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: init.defaultBranch
+  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main
+
+jobs:
+  check:
+    name: Check CI Workflow Policy
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    concurrency:
+      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-check
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Setup Node.js
+        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
+        with:
+          node-version: '24.x'
+
+      - name: Check workflows
+        run: node scripts/check-ci-workflows.mjs
+
+  # The repository's own policy checker above encodes house rules; these two
+  # jobs cover what a general-purpose linter and a security auditor find. Both
+  # were absent, which is why 9 unquoted `>> $GITHUB_OUTPUT` redirects (SC2086)
+  # and 39 zizmor findings accumulated unnoticed.
+  actionlint:
+    name: actionlint
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    concurrency:
+      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-actionlint
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      # The Docker image bundles shellcheck and pyflakes, so this also lints
+      # every `run:` block. A native actionlint binary without shellcheck on
+      # PATH silently skips the shell checks and exits 0 - worth knowing when
+      # reproducing a failure locally:
+      #   docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/repo" -w /repo rhysd/actionlint:1.7.12 -color
+      - uses: docker://rhysd/actionlint:1.7.12@sha256:b1934ee5f1c509618f2508e6eb47ee0d3520686341fec936f3b79331f9315667
+        with:
+          args: -color
+
+  zizmor:
+    name: zizmor
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    concurrency:
+      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-zizmor
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      # Annotations rather than SARIF: code scanning is not enabled on every
+      # fork of this repository, and the job should fail loudly either way.
+      #
+      # `inputs` is scoped to this repository's own workflows. The action
+      # defaults to `.`, which also collects
+      # `docs/case-studies/issue-55/template-snapshots/*/.github/workflows/*` -
+      # frozen upstream copies kept as evidence for a case study. They never
+      # run, and rewriting a snapshot to satisfy an audit destroys the thing it
+      # records, so auditing them produced 53 errors and 31 warnings that no
+      # change to this repository could clear. Their findings belong upstream,
+      # and are reported there; see
+      # `dev/log/issues/81/pulls/82/analysis/root-causes.md` (RC-10).
+      #
+      # Reproduce this job locally with:
+      #   pipx run zizmor==1.30.1 --config .github/zizmor.yml \
+      #     --min-confidence low .github/workflows
+      - uses: zizmorcore/zizmor-action@v0.6.4
+        with:
+          advanced-security: false
+          annotations: true
+          config: .github/zizmor.yml
+          inputs: .github/workflows
+          # Low, not medium: artipacked and template-injection report at low
+          # confidence, so the medium floor this job used to run with hid 38
+          # checkouts that left the job token in .git/config and 10 step
+          # outputs expanded into shell text (issue #128). The checkout rule
+          # in scripts/check-ci-workflows.mjs pins the first in-repo as well.
+          min-confidence: low
+          # Named rather than left at `latest`, which is not the newest zizmor
+          # but an entry in each action release's own digest table (v0.6.2 ->
+          # 1.29.0, v0.6.4 -> 1.30.1). Naming it keeps this run and the pipx
+          # run below on one analyser and makes a bump a visible diff line.
+          # The action refuses versions missing from its table ("Unknown
+          # version"), so bump the action first.
+          version: 1.30.1
+
+      # unpinned-images is a pedantic-only audit, so the run above does not
+      # apply the `'*': hash-pin` policy to `docker://` and `container:`
+      # images. High severity and high confidence keep that one rule without
+      # the stylistic findings the pedantic persona adds.
+      - name: Audit for pedantic-only high-severity findings
+        timeout-minutes: 5
+        run: |
+          pipx run zizmor==1.30.1 --config .github/zizmor.yml \
+            --persona pedantic --min-severity high --min-confidence high \
+            .github/workflows
+
+  # === PIPELINE STATUS ===
+  # The only job that can tell "somebody pressed stop" apart from "a check ran
+  # out of time". GitHub reports a job killed by its `timeout-minutes` as
+  # cancelled rather than failed, and a run whose only casualty is a cancelled
+  # job carries the conclusion `cancelled` as well, so the failure would pass
+  # unannounced. See scripts/check-pipeline-status.sh.
+  pipeline-status:
+    name: Pipeline Status
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    concurrency:
+      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-pipeline-status
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    needs:
+      - check
+      - actionlint
+      - zizmor
+    # A status function is required here, or the gate would inherit the implicit
+    # "every dependency succeeded" condition and be skipped in exactly the runs
+    # it exists to report. `!cancelled()` keeps it out of a superseded run,
+    # where every job is cancelled and there is nothing to report.
+    if: >-
+      !cancelled()
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Setup Node.js
+        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
+        with:
+          node-version: '24.x'
+
+      - name: Fail the run when a required job was cancelled or failed
+        env:
+          NEEDS_JSON: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
+          RUN_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
+          BRANCH_NAME: ${{ github.head_ref || github.ref_name }}
+        run: bash scripts/check-pipeline-status.sh

+name: Broken Link Checker
+
+# Documentation rots quietly: a link that 404s breaks nobody's build, so nothing
+# reports it until a reader hits it. Best practice #12 -- check links in CI.
+#
+# A naive link check is itself a source of false positives, which is the very
+# thing this pipeline is meant to avoid: an unrelated pull request should not go
+# red because a third-party host had an outage or rate-limited the runner. So
+# lychee runs with fail: false and a broken link only fails the job when the
+# Wayback Machine has no archived copy either -- at which point the link really
+# is unrecoverable and the documentation needs editing.
+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches:
+      - main
+    paths:
+      - '**.md'
+      - '**.html'
+      - '.lycheeignore'
+      - '.github/workflows/links.yml'
+  pull_request:
+    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
+    paths:
+      - '**.md'
+      - '**.html'
+      - '.lycheeignore'
+      - '.github/workflows/links.yml'
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+# Provide Git config to actions/checkout itself; checkout runs git init before
+# any workflow step can configure Git.
+env:
+  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
+  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: init.defaultBranch
+  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main
+
+jobs:
+  link-checker:
+    name: Check Links
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    # Typical run: <1min with the lychee cache. 10min stops a slow external host
+    # or a Wayback Machine probe from hanging the workflow.
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    concurrency:
+      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-link-checker
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Setup Node.js
+        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
+        with:
+          node-version: '24.x'
+
+      # `--cache` below reads and writes .lycheecache in the workspace, which
+      # a fresh checkout does not have; without this step the flag did nothing
+      # and every run re-checked every link (issue #128). A key per commit
+      # saves a new entry each run, and the prefix restores the newest one;
+      # `--max-cache-age` still expires individual results.
+      - name: Restore lychee cache
+        uses: actions/cache@v5
+        with:
+          path: .lycheecache
+          key: lychee-${{ github.sha }}
+          restore-keys: lychee-
+
+      - name: Check links with lychee
+        id: lychee
+        uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@v2
+        with:
+          # dev/log holds downloaded CI logs and analysis notes that cite run
+          # URLs and issues from other repositories; they are evidence of what
+          # was investigated, not documentation to keep reachable.
+          args: >-
+            --verbose
+            --no-progress
+            --cache
+            --max-cache-age 1d
+            --max-retries 3
+            --timeout 30
+            --exclude-path dev/log
+            './**/*.md'
+            './**/*.html'

+          fail: false
+          output: lychee/out.md
+          jobSummary: true

+          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

+        env:
+          LYCHEE_OUTPUT: lychee/out.md

+          echo "  lychee found one or more broken links in the *.md and *.html files of this repository."
+          echo "  The Web Archive (Wayback Machine) check found no archived version for some of them."
+          echo ""
+          echo "How to fix:"
+          echo "  1. Review the 'Check links with lychee' step above for the full list of broken links."

+          echo "     replace the broken link with the suggested archive.org URL."
+          echo "  3. For links with no archived version, either:"
+          echo "     a. Point the link at the current location of the same content."
+          echo "     b. Remove the link if the content is no longer relevant."
+          echo "     c. Add the URL to .lycheeignore if it is a known false positive."
+          echo ""

+          BRANCH_NAME: ${{ github.head_ref || github.ref_name }}

+name: Repository Quality Gates
+
+# Language-agnostic gates that apply to the whole repository rather than to a
+# single implementation. Keeping them here avoids duplicating the same job in
+# js.yml, python.yml and rust.yml, where they would drift apart over time.

+    branches:
+      - main
+  pull_request:

+  contents: read

+  # #128, reproductions/secretlint-planted-secret.log); a clean tree prints
+  # nothing.
+  secrets-scan:
+    name: Secrets Scan
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04

+    concurrency:
+      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-secrets-scan
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Setup Node.js
+        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
+        with:
+          node-version: '24.x'
+
+      - name: Run secretlint
+        run: npx --yes -p secretlint@13.0.7 -p @secretlint/secretlint-rule-preset-recommend@13.0.7 secretlint --secretlintignore .gitignore "**/*"
+
+  # === VERSION MODIFICATION CHECK ===

+  # python and rust). A version edited by hand in a pull request either collides

+  # the changelog and the registry disagreeing. One job covers all three
+  # manifests so the rule cannot drift apart per language.

+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04

+      cancel-in-progress: true

+          persist-credentials: false
+

+        with:

+

+  # documentation and workflow file, in all three implementations.

+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    concurrency:
+      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-file-line-limits
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+        with:

+          RUN_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
+          BRANCH_NAME: ${{ github.head_ref || github.ref_name }}

+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+    paths:
+      - 'js/**'
+      - 'python/**'
+      - 'rust/**'
+      - '.github/workflows/safari.yml'
+  push:
+    branches: [main]
+    paths:
+      - 'js/**'
+      - 'python/**'
+      - 'rust/**'
+      - '.github/workflows/safari.yml'
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+env:
+  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
+  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: init.defaultBranch
+  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main
+
+jobs:
+  smoke:
+    name: Safari (${{ matrix.language }})
+    runs-on: macos-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 30
+    strategy:
+      fail-fast: false
+      matrix:
+        language: [javascript, python, rust]
+    concurrency:
+      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-${{ matrix.language }}
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    env:

+      CARGO_BUILD_JOBS: '2'

+          driver_setup=$!

+      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
+        if: matrix.language == 'javascript'
+        with:
+          node-version: '24.x'
+      - name: Install JavaScript dependencies
+        if: matrix.language == 'javascript'
+        working-directory: js
+        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

+        working-directory: js
+        run: node scripts/run-tests.mjs tests/e2e/safari.e2e.test.js
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
+        if: matrix.language == 'python'
+        with:
+          python-version: '3.13'
+      - name: Install Python dependencies
+        if: matrix.language == 'python'
+        run: python -m pip install -e 'python[dev]'
+      - name: Exercise Python Safari commands
+        if: matrix.language == 'python'
+        working-directory: python

+      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@683b588c487a69d01f6c6ddf40f036ff682cc2c8 # v1

+      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2.9.2

+name: Security
+
+# Nothing in this repository looked at a dependency tree or at the source from a
+# security angle: `npm audit` ran only as an advisory line inside the JS release
+# job, `cargo audit` and a Python audit ran nowhere, and no static analysis was
+# configured at all. Three npm advisories therefore sat in the committed lock
+# file until this pull request. Best practice #7 -- audit dependencies on a
+# schedule, not only when somebody remembers.
+#
+# The audits run per language directory because this is a monorepo: js/,
+# python/ and rust/ each carry their own manifest and lock file.
+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches:
+      - main
+  pull_request:
+    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
+  schedule:
+    # Monday 06:00 UTC. A new advisory against an unchanged lock file is the
+    # normal case, so waiting for the next push would hide it indefinitely.
+    - cron: '0 6 * * 1'
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  # Read-only by default; the jobs that upload findings or comment on a pull
+  # request opt into the extra scopes they need in their own blocks.
+  contents: read
+
+env:
+  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
+  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: init.defaultBranch
+  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main
+
+jobs:
+  codeql:
+    name: CodeQL (${{ matrix.language }})
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 30
+    concurrency:
+      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-codeql-${{ matrix.language }}
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    permissions:
+      actions: read
+      contents: read
+      security-events: write
+    strategy:
+      fail-fast: false
+      matrix:
+        # `actions` covers the workflows themselves, which is where this
+        # repository's CI/CD defects actually lived.
+        language: [javascript-typescript, python, rust, actions]
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Initialize CodeQL
+        uses: github/codeql-action/init@v4
+        with:
+          languages: ${{ matrix.language }}
+          # No-build analysis is supported for every language in this matrix
+          # and makes the CodeQL paths-ignore configuration apply to Rust too.
+          build-mode: none
+          config-file: ./.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml
+
+      - name: Analyze
+        uses: github/codeql-action/analyze@v4
+
+  dependency-review:
+    name: Dependency Review
+    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    concurrency:
+      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-dependency-review
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+      pull-requests: write
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      # `actions/dependency-review-action` fails outright - "Dependency review
+      # is not supported on this repository" - when the dependency graph is off,
+      # which it is here: the same token reads
+      # `/repos/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/dependency-graph/sbom`
+      # but gets 404 for this repository. A job that can only ever be red is the
+      # false positive this pull request exists to remove, and deleting the job
+      # would trade it for a silent gap, so the availability is probed first and
+      # the miss is reported as a warning a maintainer can act on. Enabling
+      # Settings -> Code security -> Dependency graph turns the review on with
+      # no further change here.
+      - name: Check whether the dependency graph is enabled
+        id: probe
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+          REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
+          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
+          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
+        run: |
+          # `gh api --silent` exits 0 only on a 2xx, so the exit status is the
+          # whole test; the response body is of no interest here.
+          if gh api "repos/${REPOSITORY}/dependency-graph/compare/${BASE_SHA}...${HEAD_SHA}" --silent; then
+            echo 'dependency graph: available'
+            echo "available=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          else
+            echo 'dependency graph: unavailable'
+            echo "available=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+            echo "::warning title=Dependency review skipped::The dependency graph is disabled for ${REPOSITORY}, so actions/dependency-review-action cannot run. Enable Settings -> Code security -> Dependency graph. The npm, cargo and pip-audit jobs in this workflow still cover published advisories."
+          fi
+
+      - name: Review dependency changes
+        if: steps.probe.outputs.available == 'true'
+        uses: actions/dependency-review-action@v5
+        with:
+          fail-on-severity: high
+          comment-summary-in-pr: on-failure
+
+  npm-audit:
+    name: Audit npm lock
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    defaults:
+      run:
+        working-directory: js
+    concurrency:
+      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-npm-audit
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
+        with:
+          node-version: '24.x'
+
+      # `--package-lock-only` audits what is committed, with no install and no
+      # install scripts, so the gate cannot be influenced by the packages it is
+      # auditing.
+      - name: Audit current lock
+        run: npm audit --package-lock-only --audit-level=high
+
+      # The published range can resolve differently from this repository's
+      # lock (issue #164). Audit a fresh consumer of the actual packed package.
+      - name: Audit fresh packed consumer
+        run: bash ../experiments/issue-164/audit-consumer.sh
+
+      - name: Check shared Links Notation consumer
+        run: bash ../experiments/issue-168/check-consumer.sh
+
+  cargo-audit:
+    name: Cargo audit
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 15
+    defaults:
+      run:
+        working-directory: rust
+    concurrency:
+      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-cargo-audit
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@5bf6ce016fd2e72eefc647cbca1e4213f65955b8 # v2.87.5
+        with:
+          tool: cargo-audit@0.22.2
+
+      - name: Audit committed Cargo.lock
+        run: cargo audit --file Cargo.lock --deny warnings
+
+  python-audit:
+    name: Audit Python dependencies
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 15
+    defaults:
+      run:
+        working-directory: python
+    concurrency:
+      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-python-audit
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Setup Python
+        uses: actions/setup-python@v6
+        with:
+          python-version: '3.13'
+
+      # The package pins no lock file, so the audit resolves every declared
+      # extra into a throwaway environment and audits that.
+      - name: Audit pyproject.toml
+        run: python scripts/audit_dependencies.py
+
+  # === PIPELINE STATUS ===
+  # The only job that can tell "somebody pressed stop" apart from "a check ran
+  # out of time". GitHub reports a job killed by its `timeout-minutes` as
+  # cancelled rather than failed, and a run whose only casualty is a cancelled
+  # job carries the conclusion `cancelled` as well, so the failure would pass
+  # unannounced. See scripts/check-pipeline-status.sh.
+  pipeline-status:
+    name: Pipeline Status
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    concurrency:
+      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-pipeline-status
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    needs:
+      - codeql
+      - dependency-review
+      - npm-audit
+      - cargo-audit
+      - python-audit
+    # A status function is required here, or the gate would inherit the implicit
+    # "every dependency succeeded" condition and be skipped in exactly the runs
+    # it exists to report. `!cancelled()` keeps it out of a superseded run,
+    # where every job is cancelled and there is nothing to report.
+    if: >-
+      !cancelled()
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+
+      - name: Setup Node.js
+        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
+        with:
+          node-version: '24.x'
+
+      - name: Fail the run when a required job was cancelled or failed
+        env:
+          NEEDS_JSON: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
+          RUN_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
+          BRANCH_NAME: ${{ github.head_ref || github.ref_name }}
+        run: bash scripts/check-pipeline-status.sh

+# zizmor configuration for the workflow security audit run by
+# `.github/workflows/ci-policy.yml`.
+#
+# Blanket policy: third-party actions must be pinned to a commit hash, because
+# a mutable tag or branch of a repository we do not control is arbitrary code
+# execution in any job that holds credentials. Namespaces we do trust to keep
+# their release tags immutable are allowed to stay on a readable ref.
+rules:
+  unpinned-uses:
+    config:
+      policies:
+        actions/*: ref-pin
+        github/*: ref-pin
+        docker/*: ref-pin
+        astral-sh/*: ref-pin
+        lycheeverse/*: ref-pin
+        zizmorcore/*: ref-pin
+        '*': hash-pin

+# Lychee ignore patterns - regex patterns for URLs to skip during link checking
+#
+# Add patterns here for:
+# - Local/placeholder URLs
+# - URLs that require authentication
+# - Known false positives (rate-limited sites, etc.)
+# - URLs intentionally used as examples
+
+# Localhost and local development URLs
+http://localhost
+https://localhost
+http://127.0.0.1
+https://127.0.0.1
+
+# Example/placeholder URLs commonly used in documentation
+https://example\.com
+http://example\.com
+
+# npm.js returns 403 to link checkers (bot protection)
+https://www\.npmjs\.com
+
+# Medium.com returns 403 to link checkers (bot protection)
+https://medium\.com
+
+# Web Archive returns 502 to link checkers (bot protection)
+https://web\.archive\.org
+
+# Browser-internal pages (chrome://version, edge://welcome-edge, …) are named in
+# the docs as places to look, not fetchable links; lychee reports each as an
+# unsupported URL scheme (issue #128).
+^(chrome|edge)://

+# Local quality gates, so that "green on my machine" means the same thing as
+# "green in CI" (CI/CD best practice #8).
+#
+# Every `repo: local` hook below runs the exact command the corresponding
+# workflow step runs, and `js/tests/unit/pre-commit-config.test.js` fails if the
+# two ever drift apart. A hook that runs something *similar* to CI is worse than
+# no hook: it teaches contributors to trust a check that does not match the one
+# that will actually block their pull request.
+#
+# Install once per clone:
+#   pip install pre-commit && pre-commit install
+#
+# Run everything by hand:
+#   pre-commit run --all-files
+#
+# Skip a slow hook for one commit (it still runs in CI):
+#   SKIP=rust-clippy git commit ...
+
+# Frozen evidence: verbatim upstream snapshots and downloaded CI logs are kept
+# byte-for-byte on purpose, so no hook may reformat them.
+exclude: |
+  (?x)^(
+    docs/case-studies/[^/]+/template-snapshots/.*|
+    docs/case-studies/[^/]+/(ci-logs|ci-metadata|analysis-artifacts)/.*|
+    docs/case-studies/[^/]+/.*\.(log|txt)|
+    dev/log/.*|
+    ci-logs/.*|
+    js/package-lock\.json|
+    rust/Cargo\.lock
+  )$
+
+repos:
+  - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks
+    rev: v5.0.0
+    hooks:
+      - id: trailing-whitespace
+      - id: end-of-file-fixer
+      - id: check-yaml
+      - id: check-json
+      - id: check-toml
+      - id: check-merge-conflict
+      - id: check-added-large-files
+      - id: detect-private-key
+
+  - repo: local
+    hooks:
+      # --- JavaScript: mirrors the lint job in .github/workflows/js.yml ---
+      - id: js-eslint
+        name: ESLint (js/)
+        entry: bash -c 'cd js && npm run lint'
+        language: system
+        files: ^js/.*\.(js|mjs|cjs)$
+        pass_filenames: false
+
+      - id: js-prettier
+        name: Prettier (js/)
+        entry: bash -c 'cd js && npm run format:check'
+        language: system
+        files: ^js/
+        pass_filenames: false
+
+      - id: js-duplication
+        name: jscpd duplication baseline (js/)
+        entry: bash -c 'cd js && npm run check:duplication'
+        language: system

+## Profiles
+
+Without a user data directory every launch gets a fresh temporary profile that
+is deleted on close. With an explicit one,
+a profile directory is permanent storage: all cookies, session ones included, survive restarts.
+Session cookies (cookies without an expiry date, which most logins set) are
+kept by the browser's own encrypted cookie store; Browser Commander writes no
+plaintext copy of them.
+
+- **Chromium** (Chrome, Edge, Brave, Chromium, Chrome for Testing) launches
+  with `--restore-last-session`. The last session's tabs are deleted first, so
+  a launch still starts with one tab; `restoreTabs` reopens them.
+- **Firefox** under a WebDriver engine starts with
+  `browser.startup.page = 3` ("Open previous windows and tabs"), and the
+  restored tabs are closed after launch.
+- **Safari**, an attached browser and an explicitly selected
+  chromium-headless-shell cannot keep them: the launch result carries a
+  `warnings` entry instead.
+- `keepSessionCookies: false` (`keep_session_cookies=False` in Python,
+  `.keep_session_cookies(false)` in Rust, `--no-keep-session-cookies` in the
+  CLI) restores Chromium's default of deleting session cookies at startup.
+  Temporary profiles behave as before.
+- `persistentProfileArgs()` returns the switches for apps that start the
+  browser themselves and attach over CDP.

+## Local Quality Gates
+
+The same checks CI runs are available as git pre-commit hooks, so a commit that
+would fail the pipeline fails on the machine that wrote it instead. Every hook in
+[`.pre-commit-config.yaml`](.pre-commit-config.yaml) runs the exact command its
+workflow runs, and `js/tests/unit/scripts/pre-commit-config.test.js` fails if the
+two ever drift apart.
+
+Install once per clone:
+
+```bash
+pip install pre-commit
+pre-commit install
+```
+
+Run everything by hand, without committing:
+
+```bash
+pre-commit run --all-files
+```
+
+A hook only runs when a file it covers is staged: editing `python/` never waits
+for Clippy. A single slow hook can be skipped for one commit with
+`SKIP=rust-clippy git commit ...`, and CI will still run it.

+# Issue #112 / PR #113 — CI/CD signal audit
+
+Evidence: `issue.json`, and `ci-logs/run-<id>.{json,log}` for all 10 runs listed in the issue
+(commit `6764d1f` on `main`, plus Browser Parity `25b7191`).
+
+## Timeline
+
+1. 2026-10-01 ~19:00Z — PR #111 merged as `6764d1f`; nine workflows start.
+2. 19:03Z — JS pipeline releases `0.21.1` (`b52749c`). Lint step passes with one ESLint warning.
+3. 19:04Z — Python Auto Release builds the wheel, PyPI OIDC exchange fails with `invalid-publisher`; Pipeline Status fails.
+4. 19:20Z — Rust Auto Release: push rejected once (main advanced from the JS release), rebases, publishes `0.14.0` (`863eeca`) with a cargo `--token` deprecation warning.
+5. Issue #112 opened listing one failing run.
+
+## Requirements
+
+| # | Requirement | Status |
+|---|---|---|
+| R1 | Find and fix every error in CI/CD | Only error: PyPI trusted publisher (F1) — account-side, not fixable in code |
+| R2 | Find and fix every warning | F2–F4 fixed; F5–F7 external/intentional (below) |
+| R3 | Find false positives / negatives | F2 (lint passes with warnings) was a false negative; fixed |
+| R4 | Compare with the JS/Rust/Python templates; report shared problems upstream | F4 also in the Rust template → reported |
+| R5 | Follow hive-mind CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES | Zero-warning gates, no secrets in argv, explicit script allowlists |

+| ID | Signal (log) | Root cause | Resolution |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| F1 | `run-36911106264.log:4365` `invalid-publisher` | `browser-commander` is not on PyPI and no *pending* trusted publisher is registered for `link-foundation/browser-commander`, `python.yml`, no environment. Same finding as issues #83/#99; `scripts/explain_pypi_failure.py` already prints the exact form values. | **Maintainer action**: register the pending publisher at https://pypi.org/manage/account/publishing/ and re-run. Kept as a hard failure (correct positive). |
+| F2 | `run-36911106131.log` `530:8 warning Async function 'launchAndConnectRealBrowserWithDependencies' has a complexity of 31` | Function grew past the limit; `npm run lint` was `eslint .`, which exits 0 on warnings, so CI stayed green (false negative). | Extracted `removingTemporaryProfileOnError()` in `js/src/browser/real-browser.js`; lint is now `eslint . --max-warnings 0`. Verified: old code → exit 1, new code → exit 0. |

Verified locally: 4 warning lines without the entry, 0 with it. |
+| F4 | `run-36911106321.log:14604` ``cargo publish --token` is deprecated`` | `rust/scripts/publish-crate.mjs` passed the token as a flag. | Token now exported as `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` (also keeps it out of argv). Upstream: https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/177. Check: `experiments/issue-112-no-cargo-token-flag.mjs`. |

+# Requirements, research and implementation plan
+
+Scope: [#122](https://github.com/link-foundation/browser-commander/issues/122),
+all five sub-issues, their comments, and the reopening comment on #114.
+The checkout starts at 0.23.0 (JS), 0.5.3 (Python), 0.16.0 (Rust).
+The repository's CLAUDE.md names an obsolete issue/branch; the current user's
+explicit branch instruction takes precedence. No AGENTS.md was found.
+
+## Execution checklist
+
+- [x] Read the parent, five children and #114 including all comments.
+- [x] Read PR #123 conversation, inline comments and reviews (none at start).
+- [x] Review recent merged work (#115, #116) and existing native implementations.
+- [x] Research upstream formats and libraries; record sources and tradeoffs.
+- [x] Add failing minimum reproductions for the implemented fixes before changing code.
+- [x] Apply implemented fixes to JS, Python, Rust and CLI/command-stream/launch paths.
+- [ ] Complete every remaining feature in all five sub-issues.
+- [x] Validate implemented source immutability, domain isolation, encryption and diagnostics with fixtures.
+- [x] Generate capability matrices from shared byte-identical declarations and check them in CI.
+- [x] Run local CI checks and all tests; keep large logs outside tracked code.
+- [x] Add release fragments and commit atomic work.
+- [x] Push only the prepared branch.
+- [x] Review PR diff for regressions and synchronize current main.
+- [x] Replace WIP title/body with accurate implementation and validation evidence.
+- [x] Verify CI timestamps and head SHA; preserve/analyze failing logs and record fixes.
+- [x] Commit the reviewed changes and check a clean working tree.
+- [ ] Mark PR ready after every requirement and required check passes.
+
+## CI recovery on October 5
+
+- [x] Verify current-head run timestamps, all issue/comments and default-branch ancestry.
+- [x] Save available logs, job metadata and check annotations under `ci-logs/`.
+- [x] Match unassigned jobs to GitHub's hosted-runner incident; rerun failed jobs.
+- [x] Reproduce the shared status gate accepting `abandoned` and missing results.
+- [x] Reject unexpected results in the shared gate; preserve cancellation handling.
+- [x] Complete local checks and commit the regression tests, gate and documentation.
+- [ ] Verify every workflow and aggregate CodeQL check on the updated head.
+- [ ] Update PR evidence and recheck default-branch ancestry and a clean working tree.
+
+All twelve originally cancelled jobs had no runner or executed steps. GitHub's
+[hosted-runner incident](https://www.githubstatus.com/incidents/3q1yb5m7ltvb)
+started before the affected runs. Rerunning the same commit recovered some
+workflows; others again failed before runner acquisition. Their status logs also
+revealed an undocumented `abandoned` dependency result that the shared gate
+accepted as success. The fix rejects unknown/missing results in all ten workflows
+without replacing dependencies or increasing timeouts. The full feature scope
+below remains individually tracked and incomplete.
+
+## Complete requirement inventory and candidate solutions
+
+Each row is a requirement, including acceptance criteria. These are plans, not
+claims that every capability has shipped. `Implemented` means the specific native
+behavior is covered by fixtures in all three languages; platform acceptance is
+tracked separately. `Partial` identifies requirements whose entire scope is not
+implemented. `Pending` is unimplemented, not resolved by rejecting the option.
+Unsupported platform capabilities must be explicit in the report and matrix.

+{"body":"## Goal

From **any installed browser** it must be possible to do a **full import** or a **cross import** into **any browser instance Browser Commander controls**, in JS, Rust and Python with identical options, and from the CLI (reachable through command-stream). A fresh, clean profile stays the default; import is opt-in.

- **Full import**: same-engine clone of everything the browser stores, so the controlled instance is as close as possible to the user's real one (Chrome → controlled Chrome, Firefox → controlled Firefox, Safari → controlled WebKit where possible).
- **Cross import**: translate data between engines (Safari → Chromium, Chrome → Firefox, Firefox → WebKit, ...), every data class the target can hold.

## What exists today (0.21.2)

- Sources: `chrome`, `chromium`, `brave`, `edge`, `firefox` (`SUPPORTED_COOKIE_BROWSERS`, `migration/index.js`).
- Target: a **Chromium** profile only (Firefox data is converted to Chrome formats, `firefoxBookmarksToChrome`). Controlled Firefox/WebKit instances cannot receive an import.
- Data classes: `cookies`, `bookmarks`, `history`, `passwords`, `preferences`, `extensions`.

## Missing

### Sources
- **Safari** and Safari Technology Preview: cookies from `~/Library/Containers/com.apple.Safari/Data/Library/Cookies/Cookies.binarycookies` (fallback `~/Library/Cookies/Cookies.binarycookies`; documented, unencrypted format), `Bookmarks.plist`, `History.db`, LocalStorage/IndexedDB under the Safari container. Passwords live in the iCloud Keychain and cannot be read directly: offer the documented path (Safari / Passwords app "Export Passwords" CSV, then import that CSV) instead of silently skipping.
- Other Chromium browsers: **Opera, Opera GX, Vivaldi, Arc, Yandex, Chrome Beta/Dev/Canary, Edge Beta/Dev**, any custom `userDataDir`. The format is the Chromium one; mostly profile-root paths plus each browser's Keychain/DPAPI/libsecret key name.
- Firefox forks: **LibreWolf, Waterfox, Zen, Floorp, Firefox Developer Edition / Nightly** (profiles.ini locations).
- **Default browser**: `browser: 'default'` / `'auto'` resolves the system default (existing `system-browser.js` detection) and, for a `domains` request, falls back to other installed browsers that hold cookies for those domains, reporting which one was used.

### Targets
- Import into a controlled **Firefox** instance (cookies.sqlite / via BiDi or the CDP-less path, places.sqlite, logins.json + key4.db re-encryption, prefs.js, extensions where signing allows).
- Import into a controlled **WebKit** instance (Playwright WebKit: cookies via `context.addCookies`, storage state for localStorage/IndexedDB; persistent-context files where supported).
- Same-engine **full clone** mode for every engine: copy the whole profile (snapshot of a locked profile, as `attach snapshot` does), re-keying encrypted stores for the controlled instance, so nothing is lost by translation.

### Data classes
Add to the existing six:
- `localStorage`, `indexedDB`, `sessionStorage` (many sites keep their sign-in there, not only in cookies)
- `autofill` (addresses; payment cards only behind an explicit flag)
- `searchEngines`, `siteSettings`/permissions, `openTabs`/sessions, `downloads` history, `readingList`, client certificates where the OS allows
- **Passkeys**: not exportable from iCloud Keychain / Google Password Manager / Windows Hello by design. Report them as a skipped class with that reason, and document the supported path (sign in once in the controlled instance with the platform passkey; the persistent profile keeps the session).

### Behaviour
- Every class reports `migrated` / `skipped` (with reason) / `warnings` per source and target, as today.
- `domains` filtering applies to every class that is per-site (cookies, storage, passwords, history, permissions).
- Clear errors for OS protection: macOS Full Disk Access for Safari's container (`EPERM`; name the app that needs it and offer `x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_AllFiles`), Keychain prompts for Chromium Safe Storage keys, locked profiles (use the snapshot path).
- `cookies sources --domain <d>` / `profile sources`: which installed browsers and profiles hold data for a domain (names and counts only, never values), so callers can ask "import your github.com sign-in from Safari?" before reading anything.
- A source × target × data-class support matrix in the README, generated from the code and checked in CI, the same in all three languages.

### Tests
Fixture profiles for every source family (Chromium, Firefox, Safari `.binarycookies`/plist/sqlite) and round-trip tests into every target engine; parity tests across JS, Rust and Python; the EPERM and locked-profile paths.

Consumer: link-foundation/package-registry-manager#26 (reuse an existing registry/GitHub sign-in so crates.io/npm/PyPI publishing needs no manual login).


## Linked implementation work

The reopening comment permits splitting remaining requirements into linked issues.
PR #116 implements Safari/Safari Technology Preview **cookie** sources for the
existing Chromium import target, plus source/default/custom discovery and Safari
cookie Full Disk Access guidance. It does not close this tracking issue.

- [ ] #117 — Safari non-cookie sources (plist/sqlite/password CSV), modern named profiles and WebsiteDataStore paths.
- [ ] #118 — Firefox/WebKit import targets and same-engine full profile clones.
- [ ] #119 — Storage, autofill, settings, sessions, downloads, reading list, certificates and explicit passkey reporting; per-site domains filtering.
- [ ] #120 — Remaining protection/lock diagnostics, discovery and the generated source × target × data-class support matrix with native parity/round-trip tests.

Keep #114 open until the complete import goal and the acceptance criteria in these linked issues have shipped.

+{"body":"## Goal

Every popular desktop browser, at least as popular as Yandex Browser and Opera, must be fully supported, the same in JS, Rust and Python and through the CLI. That means it can be **launched and controlled**, **attached to**, **imported from**, **detected as the default browser** and **protected** (never run on its own default profile).

## Audit of `main` (0.22.0)

The import catalogue `browser-sources.json` (identical in all three languages) has chrome (+beta/dev/canary), chromium, edge (+beta/dev), brave, vivaldi, opera, opera-gx, yandex, arc, firefox (+developer/nightly), librewolf, waterfox, zen and floorp, with default-browser ids. Everything else lags behind it:

### 1. Launch and control: only Chrome, Chromium, Edge and Brave
`CHANNEL_EXECUTABLE_NAMES` and the macOS/Windows executable tables (`js/src/browser/system-browser.js`, `rust/src/browser/system_browser.rs`, `python/.../system_browser.py`) know only chrome*, chromium, msedge* and brave. Missing from launch, `channel` and `attach`:
- **Opera, Opera GX**: `Opera.app/Contents/MacOS/Opera`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Opera\opera.exe` (per-user install; also launcher.exe), `/usr/bin/opera`. Opera speaks CDP; OperaDriver exists for WebDriver.
- **Yandex Browser**: `Yandex.app/Contents/MacOS/Yandex`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Yandex\YandexBrowser\Application\browser.exe`, `/usr/bin/yandex-browser(-stable)`.
- **Vivaldi**: `Vivaldi.app/Contents/MacOS/Vivaldi`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Vivaldi\Application\vivaldi.exe`, `/usr/bin/vivaldi(-stable)`.
- **Arc**: `Arc.app/Contents/MacOS/Arc`.
- **Naver Whale**, **360 Secure/Extreme**, **QQ Browser** (see 3).
- **Firefox family**: stock Firefox and its forks can be driven through WebDriver BiDi (Puppeteer supports it; Playwright needs its patched build). Launching an *installed* Firefox, LibreWolf, Waterfox, Zen or Floorp should work through the BiDi path.
- **Safari**: control through `safaridriver` (WebDriver; needs "Allow Remote Automation"), so Safari is not limited to import.

The launch tables should come from the same catalogue (add `executables` per platform to `browser-sources.json`), so the source list and the launch list cannot drift apart again.

### 2. Default-profile protection is missing for most browsers
`knownDefaultUserDataDirs` (refuses to launch on a browser's own profile: "requires a dedicated userDataDir, not a browser default profile") lists only Chrome, Chromium, Brave and Edge. Launching Yandex, Opera, Vivaldi, Arc etc. with their real profile directory is not refused. Derive it from the catalogue `roots` too.

### 3. Popular browsers missing from the catalogue
- **Naver Whale** (Korea): macOS `~/Library/Application Support/Naver/Whale`, Windows `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Naver\Naver Whale\User Data`, Linux `~/.config/naver-whale`; `Whale Safe Storage`.
- **360 Secure Browser / 360 Extreme Browser** (China, Windows): `%APPDATA%\360se6\User Data`, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\360Chrome\Chrome\User Data`.
- **QQ Browser** (China, Windows): `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Tencent\QQBrowser\User Data`.
- **Sogou Explorer** (China, Windows): `%APPDATA%\SogouExplorer`.
- **DuckDuckGo** (macOS WebKit, Windows WebView2) and **Tor Browser** (Firefox ESR inside its bundle): at least detection, plus import where the stores are readable.
- **Safari** (still open in #114).
- Samsung Internet and UC Browser are mobile-only, so they are out of scope for desktop control. Document that.

### 4. Yandex passwords
Yandex Browser stores saved passwords in `Ya Passman Data` (not `Login Data`), with an extra encryption layer: a key in the `meta` table (`local_encryptor_data`), protected by the os_crypt key, and an optional master password. Today password import from Yandex will report `source-missing`. Support it, or report a specific skipped reason. Also check Yandex `Cookies` with a fixture.

### 5. Opera specifics
- Single-profile layout (`singleProfile: true`). The Windows profile is in **Roaming** (`%APPDATA%\Opera Software\Opera Stable`) while its caches and `Local State` placement differ; check that migration finds `Local State` and the cookie key on all three OSes.
- Opera's sidebar messengers and its VPN are part of the browser; launching for automation should not turn them off unless asked (same "as close to the real browser as possible" default).

### 6. Tests and parity
- A support matrix in the README (browser × launch / attach / import / default detection / protection × OS), generated from the catalogue and checked in CI.
- Fixture tests for each new source (Whale, 360, QQ, Sogou, Yandex `Ya Passman Data`, Opera on each OS).
- The same behaviour in JS, Rust and Python, and through `browser-commander` CLI subcommands (reachable from command-stream).

Related: #114 (Safari, non-Chromium targets, data classes); link-foundation/package-registry-manager#30 (consumer: source and channel lists).

+
+## Narrative per actionable finding
+
+**1. Safari JS smoke cancelled (known).** One test was cancelled because the
+test HTTP server's `close()` never resolved: Safari keeps an idle preconnect
+socket open and Node 24's `server.close()` waits for it. The Pipeline Status
+gate correctly reported `Failing jobs: smoke` (safari:1924-1925). The fix in
+progress is commit f2988a3.
+
+**2. Rust Windows doc-test timeout (known) plus duplicated doc tests.**
+`cargo test --all-features` without target filters already builds and runs
+doc tests. The log shows `Doc-tests browser_commander … 20 passed` inside the
+"Rust test suite" step on all three OSes. The separate "Run doc tests" step
+(rust.yml:272-276) repeats them. On Windows the second run hung until the 180s
+budget killed it (exit 124), even though the same doc tests had passed 19.46s
+earlier in the same job (rust:8773). Removing the duplicate step removes the
+failure point and saves about 30 to 90 seconds per OS. If a separate doc-test
+signal is wanted, restrict the main step with `--lib --bins --tests` instead.
+
+**3/4. PyPI trusted publishing (known) and the changelog backlog.** The
+`invalid-publisher` rejection means 0.5.3 was never published. As a result, the
+auto-release sees `CHANGELOG.md already contains version 0.5.3`, skips
+collecting, and leaves 17 fragments unreleased on every push. Registering the
+trusted publisher fixes both problems.
+
+**5. Puppeteer manifest drift test always skipped.** This is the clearest false
+negative. The test exists to catch drift between the vendored Puppeteer API
+manifest and the installed `puppeteer-core`, but it skips exactly when that
+drift exists. CI is green on three OSes while the manifest is two minor
+versions behind. Regenerate the manifest and turn the skip into a failure.
+
+**6. Unclosed sqlite connection.** Each Python test job reports `1 warning`. In
+`sqlite3`, `with connect(...) as db` manages a transaction and does not close
+the connection. The warning is raised at garbage collection in the test that
+runs next, which is why its location differs by OS. Fix the `with` blocks in
+the tests (and audit callers of `_open_cookie_database`), then promote
+`ResourceWarning` to an error.
+
+**7. Codecov never uploads.** The skip shows up only as a notice, so the job
+is green. Either configure the token or remove the step.
+
+**8. Untested e2e and ignored suites.** Several suites exist only on disk.
+Because no workflow invokes them, they can rot without any signal. Wire them
+into parity.yml, which already has a skip-detection guard, or explicitly mark
+them as manual.
+
+**9-11. Log noise.** `Command failed with exit code 7` is printed after the
+JS test summary and looks like a failure, but it is the expected rejection
+under test, echoed by command-stream's virtual `exit`. jscpd prints every
+baselined clone, which makes the lint log look broken. Both should be
+silenced so that real errors stand out.
+
+**12-17. Supply chain and hygiene warnings.** These are the DEP0005 warning
+from download-artifact@v8 (upstream; the policy is already in place), the
+`ubuntu-latest` label migration to Ubuntu 26 on 2026-10-19, unpinned zizmor
+and secretlint versions, the tag-pinned lychee action with a cache that is
+never persisted, one redirected docs link, and three browser-internal URLs
+that lychee cannot check.
+
+**18-27. Expected or noise.** No action is required beyond the optional
+improvements noted in the table.
+
+**28-39. Found while fixing.** CodeQL's open alerts on `main` are signals
+as well. Two ReDoS patterns (in JS and Python selectors, and in artifact names)
+and the hand-escaped commit message are true positives. The other alerts were
+false positives, cleared by naming and fixture changes. Running the
+previously unrun suites exposed one stale smoke test (a false negative until
+then) and an intermittent Safari back-to-back launch race. See
+`root-causes-and-solutions.md`, signals 28 to 39.

+## Verified as already in place (no action)
+
+- Every workflow has a `pipeline-status` job gated on `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}`.
+  - `scripts/check-ci-workflows.mjs` checks that its `needs:` covers every job, the equivalent of js#175.
+- Workflow-level `permissions:` are present.
+- Writer jobs share `main-writer-${{ github.repository }}-main` with `cancel-in-progress: false`.
+- `actionlint` and `zizmor` run in `ci-policy.yml`.
+- Third-party actions outside the ref-pin allowlist are hash-pinned (`.github/zizmor.yml`).
+
+## Bugs in the templates themselves (to report upstream)
+
+1. **rust template, redundant doc-test step.** `/tmp/tpl/rust/.github/workflows/release.yml:535-547` runs `cargo test --all-features --verbose` and then `cargo test --doc --verbose`.
+   - The first command already runs the lib doctests.
+   - The second, run without `--all-features`, changes the feature set. In any downstream crate that declares features, the crate is recompiled (proved in `/tmp/repro128/doccrate`).
+   - In browser-commander this cost a red main build: Windows took more than 180s and exited 124 (`ci-logs/rust-37509328352.log:8788-8791`).
+   - Fix: remove the step, or pass `--all-features`.
+2. **rust template budget wrapper, misleading comment.** `/tmp/tpl/rust/scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh:70-71` claims "A root command that exits while a worker survives therefore cannot fake completion".
+   - But `command_is_running` returns "done" as soon as the status file exists, so the wrapper still exits 0 with live group members.
+   - Only the pipe-hang half of rust#172 is fixed, and nothing reports the survivors on the success path.
+   - Fix: after completion, call `report_survivors` (or fail) when `group_members` is non-empty.
+3. **rust template, runner labels.** It still uses `ubuntu-latest` 34 times. js#193 and py#89 pinned `ubuntu-24.04`, but there is no rust equivalent, and the Ubuntu 26 migration starts on 2026-10-19.
+4. **js template, inconsistent zizmor versions.** `/tmp/tpl/js/.github/workflows/workflows.yml:116` pins the action at `version: 1.29.0`, while line 130 runs `pipx run zizmor==1.30.0`. One audit job uses two zizmor versions.
+5. **rust template, unpinned secretlint.** `/tmp/tpl/rust/.github/workflows/release.yml:241` uses `npx --yes -p secretlint ...` with no version. That is the adhoc-package pattern that zizmor flags elsewhere in the templates, and it contradicts the templates' own pinning principle.
